name: Priority Access
tagline: Protect reserved and accessible spaces before the fallback.
brief: Serve reserved, accessible, VIP, electric, large, and ordinary arrivals in a safe order.
context: The facility contains reserved, accessible, premium, charging, large, and standard spaces.
narrative:
Priority vehicles now share the entrance with ordinary traffic. Reserved vehicles need their reserved space, permit holders need accessible parking, and VIP vehicles should use premium spaces.

The controller must handle these protected cases before it reaches the ordinary vehicle-type fallback.
objective: Serve all ten vehicles and keep every protected category correctly matched.
learningObjective: Design an ordered policy that protects hard requirements before general allocation.
intelligenceExplanation:
The starter policy understands electric, large, and standard vehicles. It does not yet handle reservations, accessibility permits, or VIP access.

Add the protected cases above the existing vehicle rules so they are not captured by the broad standard fallback.
hint: Add reserved, accessible, and VIP rules above the existing electric, large, and standard rules.
hints: Reserved, accessible, and VIP conditions are visible only for the head vehicle.
The first matching rule wins; all special cases belong above hasWaitingVehicle.
A complete order is reserved, accessible, VIP, electric, large, standard, idle.

goals.description: Protect special access while serving the complete queue.

rules.description: Authorize completed stays through the exit checkpoint.
Send large vehicles to large bays.
Use standard parking for the general case.
